entries.description: Use similarity to a characterized system to form bounded explanations. Choose which sequence, local structural machinery, domain architecture, genomic context or organismal circumstance makes the reference informative for the disputed property; revise misleading comparators.
entries.name: Choose a relevant analogue and bound what transfers

entries.description: Treat an implication as something that can fail. Prefer feature/function discordance: feature without function challenges sufficiency; function without feature challenges necessity.
entries.name: Seek cases that break a proposed predictor

entries.description: Keep the candidate system explicit while choosing substrates, co-substrates or acceptors that distinguish competing recognition hypotheses. Refine the candidate space using identified products and bounded non-products.
entries.name: Discriminate competing inputs by their predicted chemistry

entries.description: After a competent negative or contradiction, separate the part of the explanation that failed from independently supported constraints. Reopen alternatives within surviving constraints without either preserving the whole annotation or discarding everything.
entries.name: Revise the failed attachment while retaining independent constraints

entries.description: Use a supported output or requirement to distinguish loss of function, unfamiliar replacement, different route and changed demand. Evaluate candidate similarities and context against these system explanations.
entries.name: Constrain missing-function hypotheses by what the system must accomplish

entries.description: Keep a real aggregate output separate from its attribution. Compare direct chemistry, substrate/cofactor supply, enabling a complex, downstream filtering and production of an observable signal.
entries.name: Retain the system output and revise who contributes what

entries.description: An improved endpoint can repair the proposed molecular relationship, use another route, reduce demand or change downstream consequences. Compare those explanations before treating rescue as mechanistic equivalence.
entries.name: Distinguish restoration from bypass, compensation and reduced demand

entries.description: Investigate which enabling resource or molecular state permits a supported capability to matter. Distinguish that prerequisite from correlated stress, altered protein amount and reporter failure.
entries.name: Test the missing prerequisite behind conditional function

entries.description: Explain a missing cellular reaction by contrasting inaccessible substrate/partner, absent substrate, failed catalyst and failed reporter delivery. Prefer changes that discriminate the relevant barrier.
entries.name: Separate physical access from chemical competence

entries.description: Choose an explicit account of matter, electrons, cofactors and energy needed for a conversion. Reopen incomplete boundaries when an isolated reaction is implausible or replacement changes metabolic demand.
entries.name: Account for the coupled chemical system

entries.description: Keep feasibility or measured capacity separate from native use. Contrast ordinary use, conditional backup, side activity and unused capacity without forcing a single-role explanation.
entries.name: Distinguish a possible route from the route actually used

entries.description: Choose time/phase contrasts distinguishing transient acceleration, repeated function, adaptation and survival. An early benefit or first product need not predict later outcomes.
entries.name: Compare biological consequences over the time that matters

entries.description: Ask whether pooled change reflects uniform effects, selective subsets or changed mixtures. Choose biologically meaningful units whose contrasts separate those explanations.
entries.name: Resolve an aggregate claim at the biological level that separates explanations

entries.description: Treat bands, cofactor changes, substrate loss and downstream signals as compatible with several transformations. Prefer evidence separating intended chemistry from half-reactions, spontaneous conversion or artifacts.
entries.name: Distinguish the transformation from its proxy readout

entries.description: Preserve demonstrated recognition, binding, cleavage or delivery when productive output fails. Compare the additional compatibility or coupling explanations rather than repeat upstream positives.
entries.name: Hold upstream success while investigating downstream failure

entries.description: Environmental responses can arise through direct ligand recognition, cofactor chemistry, changed abundance or system-demand feedback. Choose contrasts distinguishing those routes before assigning a direct sensor or regulatory sign.
entries.name: Distinguish direct input action from indirect response and feedback

entries.description: Seek comparisons preserving one property while changing another. Use their dissociation to distinguish a required functional relation from amount, delivery, stability or another linked activity.
entries.name: Separate linked functions through selective dissociation

entries.description: Compare incompatible biological claims by testing whether a difference in organism, molecular state, assay window, relation or construct predicts the disagreement. Preserve genuine conflict when available observations do not distinguish the explanations.
entries.name: Explain conflicting biological results with discriminating scope contrasts

entries.description: Preserve reproducible output after a focal loss while distinguishing another contributor from incomplete perturbation, imported product or reduced demand. Revise exclusivity without erasing the lost route’s genuine contribution.
entries.name: Investigate the route behind residual function

source_meaning: Each row links an option to the particular case observation supporting its content; no row awards credit or establishes independent replication.
